Vendored third-party assets
===========================

Everything the browser loads is served from this repository. There are no
CDN references and no network calls at runtime; each file below was
downloaded once, at build time, and committed.

That is a deliberate constraint, not an accident of packaging. The
pipeline is meant to run on a machine with no outbound access.


3D
--
three.js                r0.160.1    MIT             from unpkg.com
  build/three.module.js
  examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js
  examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js
  examples/jsm/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js


Typefaces (fonts/)
------------------
Inter                   v5.0.20     SIL OFL 1.1     via @fontsource/inter
  inter-400.woff2, inter-500.woff2, inter-600.woff2, inter-700.woff2

JetBrains Mono          v5.0.20     SIL OFL 1.1     via @fontsource/jetbrains-mono
  jetbrains-mono-400.woff2, jetbrains-mono-500.woff2

Latin subsets only. Together they are under 140 KB, which is why the
whole set can be self-hosted without thinking about it.


Libraries (lib/)
----------------
ECharts                 5.5.1       Apache-2.0      window.echarts
  Nightly throughput on the operations page and the attribute
  completeness grid on handover. Loaded only by those two pages.

Alpine.js               3.14.1      MIT             window.Alpine
  Filtering and column sorting on the work packages table, without a
  build step or a framework. Loaded only by that page.

Motion One              10.18.0     MIT             window.Motion
  Entrance animation, via the browser's native Web Animations API.
  Every animation starts from a hidden state, so static/motion.js also
  force-finishes anything still running after one second: a stalled
  animation must not be able to leave the page blank.


Build-time only (../../../../scripts/vendor/)
---------------------------------------------
Lucide                  0.451.0     ISC
  The full 347 KB icon bundle is not served. scripts/build_icon_sprite.js
  reads it and emits templates/_icons.html, a 6 KB sprite holding only
  the icons the app uses, which is inlined into the base template. So
  there is no icon library in the browser at all. Re-run that script
  after adding an icon.


Deliberately not used
---------------------
Tailwind CSS. It would need a Node toolchain and a build step on a
managed Windows machine to produce one stylesheet, and the design system
in static/app.css already provides the tokens that would justify it.
The cost is real and the benefit here is not.
